title: Migrate CommonJS utility package to ESM
description: The fixture's utility package is written in CommonJS (require/module.exports) and needs to be migrated to native ES modules (import/export) to align with the rest of the toolchain, while remaining consumable by any remaining CommonJS callers via Node's interop.
acceptanceCriteria: All source files use import/export syntax instead of require/module.exports.
package.json is updated (type: module and/or exports map) so the package resolves correctly as ESM.
A documented interop path (e.g. a generated CJS build or dual-package exports map) allows existing CommonJS callers to keep working.
All existing tests pass after the migration without behavior changes.
No remaining require() calls exist in the migrated source files, only in interop shim code if present.
verificationMethod: test-suite: run the full existing test suite post-migration, plus a repository-invariant check that no require()/module.exports remain in migrated source files.
groundTruth: Every source file's require/module.exports is converted to import/export, package.json declares type: module with an exports map, and a small CJS interop wrapper (or dual build) preserves compatibility for CommonJS consumers.
